newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. to protest over Cuba incident with diplomats.
newsitem.headline: U.S. to protest over Cuba incident with diplomats.

text.p: Washington will protest to Cuba over an incident last week in which two U.S. diplomats were verbally harassed and their vehicle tampered with after a meeting with a dissident on the island, a U.S. government source said on Monday.
Cuban Foreign Ministry officials were not immediately available to comment.

The U.S. source, who asked not to be identified, said the incident occurred last Friday after two officers from the U.S. Interests Section met a dissident journalist, Olance Nogueras, in the central port city of Cienfuegos.

The source said that as they came out of the meeting, the diplomats were filmed by a Cuban camera crew "undoubtedly from Cuban state security" and were verbally harassed, including being asked whether they felt threatened by damage to their vehicle.
The source added that one of their vehicle's tires was sabotaged and the camera crew filmed the diplomats repairing it.

The source called the incident a "clear demonstration" of President Fidel Castro's government's refusal to abide by international norms and laws of host countries' behaviour toward foreign resident diplomats.
She added Washington planned to protest over the incident, but did not give details.

Cuban authorities have sometimes expressed irritation in the past at U.S. diplomats' active contacts with dissidents on the communist-ruled island. Havana last August expelled a U.S. diplomat, saying she had violated diplomatic conventions by supporting and organising anti-government opposition groups.
The United States and Cuba, whose relations have long been hostile, do not have diplomatic ties but do have Interests Sections in each other's capital.
